title: Sickle cell disease
covers: The sickle mutation and genotypes, the acute and chronic complications (infection, splenic sequestration, pain, acute chest syndrome, stroke), screening and diagnosis, and treatment: hydroxyurea, transfusion, transplant, gene therapy and the newer drugs.

items.p: An inherited disorder with chronic hemolytic anemia, vaso-occlusive crises, organ damage and a shortened life. About 8 million people are affected, mostly where malaria is endemic.
Inheritance is autosomal recessive: two sickle genes, or one sickle gene and one thalassemia gene.
High HbF and coinherited α-thalassemia make the disease milder.
A point mutation puts valine in place of glutamic acid at position 6 of the β chain. HbS forms polymers when it loses oxygen, and the red cell sickles.

ul: Hemolysis gives anemia and fatigue
Vaso-occlusion gives pain and organ damage
Around both: inflammation, endothelial dysfunction and a tendency to clot

items.p: Lecturer's note: it is a systemic disease. Complications start in childhood and last for life: stroke, retinopathy, hearing loss, acute chest syndrome, pulmonary hypertension, gallstones, kidney damage, avascular necrosis and priapism (a painful sustained erection).

summary.h: Infection and a sudden drop in hemoglobin

items.p: The spleen stops working in early childhood. Encapsulated bacteria (pneumococcus, Haemophilus, meningococcus) and Salmonella can kill within hours. Penicillin, vaccines, newborn diagnosis and family education cut deaths.

Acute splenic sequestration is a sudden enlargement of the spleen with a hemoglobin fall of 2 g/dL or more. It can cause shock and death and recurs in up to 67%. The lecturer noted that infections trigger it. Parents are taught to feel the spleen.

table: Red cells trapped in the spleen
Parvovirus B19 stops red cell production
Donor and own cells destroyed after transfusion
Careful small-volume transfusion; splenectomy if recurrent
Transfusion; keep away from pregnant contacts

items.p: Small volumes are used in sequestration because the trapped cells return to the circulation.

Dactylitis is painful swelling of the hands and feet from vaso-occlusion of the small bones. It is often the first complication, peaks between 6 months and 2 years, and is usually bilateral (lecturer's note). Early dactylitis may signal a more severe course.
Pain is the most common complication and the top reason children with SCD use health care (not the top cause of death).

ul: Triggers: cold, stress, illness, dehydration, high altitude
Acute pain: severe, needs an unplanned visit. Chronic pain: on most days for 6 months.
Acute pain is an emergency: first analgesic within 1 hour, reassess every 30–60 minutes
Opioids titrated to effect; NSAIDs for 5–7 days; low-dose ketamine if opioids fail
Use incentive spirometry throughout to prevent acute chest syndrome

items.p: A new lung infiltrate plus chest pain, fever, fast breathing, wheeze, cough or low oxygen. It can come with a pain crisis or on its own.
It is the second cause of hospital admission and the leading cause of death in adults with SCD (mortality up to 9%).

ul: Treat with incentive spirometry, antibiotics, oxygen, careful analgesia and transfusion
Hydroxyurea reduces recurrence

items.p: Without screening, 11% of children with HbSS have a stroke by age 20, and more than half recur without treatment.

ul: Children: usually ischemic. Silent infarcts affect learning.
Adults: hemorrhagic stroke in young adults; ischemic stroke at 35–65 years
Transcranial Doppler every year from age 2 to 16 in HbSS and HbSβ⁰
At least one MRI without sedation at early school age
Velocity of 200 cm/s or more: regular transfusions cut the stroke risk by age 18 from 11% to 1.9% (STOP trial)

items.note: The handwritten note on slide 15 says the Doppler measures "cerebral artery diameter". The test measures blood flow velocity (cm/s), as on slide 16. The note "treat: ↑Hb and ↓HbSC" most likely means lowering sickle hemoglobin (HbS); HbSC is a separate genotype. Worth checking with the lecturer.

ul: Anemia is normocytic in HbSS and microcytic in HbS/β-thalassemia
Smear: sickle cells, target cells, Howell–Jolly bodies (the spleen is not working), nucleated red cells
Electrophoresis or HPLC: high HbS, often raised HbF; high HbA2 in HbS/β-thalassemia

table: Penicillin; full vaccines including pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib, flu
Stop penicillin if no splenectomy and no invasive pneumococcal infection

items.p: Today 93.9% of children with HbSS or HbSβ⁰ reach age 18. The move from pediatric to adult care is a high-risk period.
Hydroxyurea is the backbone. It raises HbF, lowers white cells and improves red cell hydration. It is safe from 9 months of age.

ul: Start early and give the maximum tolerated dose
It cuts pain crises, acute chest syndrome, admissions, transfusions and Doppler velocities
Stop it before pregnancy
REACH (2024): escalating to 20–35 mg/kg/day beat a fixed 17.5 mg/kg/day, with 79% less acute chest syndrome and no extra toxicity

table: Acute chest syndrome, sudden fall in hemoglobin, before major surgery, selected pregnancies
Stroke or abnormal Doppler, multi-organ failure, complications despite hydroxyurea

items.p: Lecturer's note: for regular transfusion, use exchange transfusion if possible. Match Rh (C, E) and K antigens to prevent alloimmunization. Watch for iron overload and hyperhemolysis. Minor surgery needs no transfusion.
Stem cell transplant is the established cure: about 95% with a matched sibling, best done young and before organ damage.

items.note: Slide 25 says about 1 in 3 patients has a matched sibling donor. Most sources give a lower figure (under 20%). Not tested in the questions.

items.p: Gene therapy (FDA, December 2023, age 12 and over) uses the patient's own stem cells, so no donor and no graft-versus-host disease. Busulfan is still needed.

table: CRISPR cuts the BCL11A switch; fetal hemoglobin turns back on
97% free of pain crises for 12 months
A viral vector adds a new β-globin gene

items.p: Newer drugs have disappointed: L-glutamine has a modest effect, crizanlizumab lost its EU approval, voxelotor was withdrawn worldwide, mitapivat gave mixed results. Lecturer's note: hydroxyurea is best.

ul: 387 patients, clustered in the North (42.5%) and South (28.4%); high consanguinity; gene influx from neighboring countries
Newborn screening of 10,095 babies: 2.1% had an abnormal hemoglobin (3.5% in the North); HbS was 81% of them, HbD 12%
Prevention: awareness, carrier screening in high school, premarital testing, prenatal or preimplantation diagnosis

Urgent, careful small-volume transfusion (trapped cells return to the circulation); splenectomy if recurrent

Cold, stress, illness, dehydration, high altitude

2nd cause of hospitalization; leading cause of death in adults with SCD

cards.a: Start by 2 months; stop at age 5 if no splenectomy and no invasive pneumococcal infection

options.E: 50%; more than 67%

questions.stem: Which stroke pattern by age matches the lecture?

questions.stem: What is the stated effect of silent cerebral infarcts in children?

options.A: They cause hemiplegia

options.E: They affect hearing

questions.stem: Under ASH 2020, who gets annual transcranial Doppler screening?

options.A: Children with HbSS or HbSβ⁰, ages 5–18
options.B: Children with HbSC or HbSβ⁺, ages 2–16
options.C: Children with HbSS or HbSβ⁰, ages 2–16
options.D: Children with any genotype, from birth to age 5
options.E: Adults with HbSS or HbSβ⁰, ages 18–35

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl with HbSS has a transcranial Doppler velocity of 210 cm/s, above the 200 cm/s cut-off. What is offered, and what did STOP show?

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with HbSS on hydroxyurea is planning a pregnancy. What does the lecture advise?

Plan ahead: preconception counseling, review medications (stop hydroxyurea), follow-up and delivery at a center with SCD expertise. A: Hydroxyurea is stopped. B: Stop it, and deliver at an expert center. C: More women with SCD are having children. D: Plan ahead, before pregnancy.

questions.stem: How does red cell size help in the diagnosis of SCD?

questions.stem: Management rests on six pillars. Which is the foundation beneath them?

E: Age 12 is the gene therapy limit.

options.D: Before major surgery

options.B: About 67%
options.C: About 50%
options.D: About 33%

questions.stem: What did the REACH trial (2024) compare in African children?

options.A: Hydroxyurea escalated to 20–35 mg/kg/day versus regular transfusion
options.B: Hydroxyurea at a fixed 17.5 mg/kg/day versus placebo
options.C: Hydroxyurea escalated to 50–70 mg/kg/day versus a fixed 35 mg/kg/day
options.D: Hydroxyurea escalated to 20–35 mg/kg/day versus a fixed 17.5 mg/kg/day
options.E: Hydroxyurea at a fixed 17.5 mg/kg/day versus L-glutamine

questions.explanation: REACH 2024: escalating to the maximum tolerated dose (20–35 mg/kg/day) beat a fixed 17.5 mg/kg/day dose. A: Both arms were hydroxyurea. B: Escalated versus fixed dose. C: 20–35 versus 17.5. E: Escalated versus fixed dose.

questions.stem: In REACH, which event fell the most at the maximum tolerated dose, and what happened to toxicity?

options.A: Acute chest syndrome, by 79%; dose-limiting toxicity did not increase
options.B: Acute chest syndrome, by 79%; dose-limiting toxicity doubled
options.C: Vaso-occlusive events, by 79%; dose-limiting toxicity did not increase
options.D: Malaria, by 79%; dose-limiting toxicity rose in malaria areas
options.E: Serious adverse events, by 40%; dose-limiting toxicity did not increase

questions.explanation: Reductions: acute chest syndrome 79%, serious adverse events 58%, non-malarial infections 48%, malaria 42%, vaso-occlusive events 40%. Dose-limiting toxicity did not increase; safe in malaria-endemic settings. B: Toxicity did not increase. C: Vaso-occlusive events fell by 40%. D: Malaria fell by 42%; it was safe there. E: Serious adverse events fell by 58%.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy with SCD recovers from a second episode of sudden pallor with a large, tender spleen. Besides teaching the parents to feel the spleen, which preventive steps does the lecture give?

options.A: Consider splenectomy; start crizanlizumab
options.B: Avoid splenectomy; start chronic steroids and penicillin
options.C: Consider transplant; stop penicillin
options.D: Avoid transfusion; start IVIG monthly
options.E: Consider splenectomy; start or optimize hydroxyurea

questions.explanation: Prevent: teach parents to feel the spleen; consider splenectomy after recurrent episodes; start or optimize hydroxyurea. A: Hydroxyurea is the step named. B: Splenectomy is considered after recurrent episodes. C: Not the steps given. D: That belongs to hyperhemolysis.
